rustPort.implementation: rust/crates/openvector/src/image_document.rs, image_pipeline.rs and palette.rs use the same Rust segmentation, smoothing and fitting kernels, with one retained CoreSession random stream. Settings/profile resolution and saved-profile persistence are implemented in settings.rs, settings_profile.rs and saved_profiles.rs.
rustPort.ownership: CoreSession and ImageDocument stay on one engine worker thread; exported DocumentSnapshot values own their buffers and may cross threads. The state() accessor borrows live raster/geometry storage for serializers. Progress observers borrow the live state with refreshed randomState/cancelled fields; observers explicitly clone it only when retaining a checkpoint. An Arc<AtomicBool> cancellation handle is checked at native progress checkpoints.
rustPort.observerCancellation: Returning the reserved image_document::CANCEL_TASK signal from a processing or export callback requests cancellation at that checkpoint and sets the document flag before unwinding. Other observer errors propagate unchanged without setting cancellation. Palette cancellation retains its current progress/status rather than manufacturing the caught vector-stage status=2 completion. A subsequent task clears cancellation according to the native stage-entry rules.
rustPort.verification: Native palette-session and settings/profile tests plus document lifecycle tests were added. Rust build, test, lint and formatting remain deferred to the integration owner; no parity pass is claimed by this implementation note.
rustPort.knownFailure: The existing encoded-PNG alpha-premultiplication discrepancy is preserved explicitly; the document pipeline does not compensate by multiplying or unpremultiplying pixels a second time.

nodeTransport.sourceReplacement: setSource decodes and validates a replacement before resetting the document. A failed replacement retains the prior rasters, processing results, settings, session random state and export eligibility. This follows the user-approved transactional preservation policy; it does not claim native failed-load equivalence.
nodeTransport.summary: Operation results and default progress checkpoints expose DocumentSummary metadata, never implicit raster, segmentation, geometry or editor-history payloads. Existing null results, cache didWork, cancellation and fitting-stage completion retain their meanings.
nodeTransport.selection: snapshot() explicitly requests all bulk sections. snapshot(selection) and progress {callback,capture} use the same SnapshotSelection: rasters names, segmentation regions/full, contours, smoothing and fitting. Metadata is always present; unrequested sections are absent; requested unavailable sections are null. Default progress capture is metadata only, drawn from the observer checkpoint rather than a reentrant document read.
nodeTransport.buffers: Raster/editor BGRA is Buffer; segmentation indices/counts/colorIndices are Int32Array; palette/referencePositions are Float32Array; byte masks are Uint8Array. Geometry retains f64 precision. Size-dependent geometry, output chains and history use direct NAPI objects and arrays, not serde_json conversion. Returned storage belongs to the caller and survives edits/reset without aliasing live engine buffers.
nodeTransport.scope: This changes Node transport only, not internal Rust-owned snapshot cloning. Explicit editing(), editingHistory() and background getters retain full typed information; editor commands return compact metadata. Frozen evidence and historical JavaScript component contracts below predate this Node transport and are not current npm API examples.
